texts.facts: 1. The present Dar (detailed accident report) arises out of an accident that occurred on 27.09.2019, resulting in grievous injury to the victim/claimant. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 27.09.2019, investigating officer ASI Kanhaiya Lal received Mustafa Kamal (Dar) vs Ajeet Singh (254/18 New Friends Colony) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87512516/ 1 DD no. 3A upon which he along with Ct.Dharambir reached the spot. About 200 steps on the road from Mathura Road-Ashram Flyover, a scooty no. DL-3SDZ-4239 was found lying in accidental condition and blood stains were found on the road. The victim was informed to have been taken to the hospital. IO clicked photographs of the scene. He received GD no. 5A regarding MLC and reached AIIMS Trauma Centre where victim/claimant was found unconscious. The concerned doctor endorsed a road traffic accident case on the MLC with the fact that the patient, driving a two wheeler, had collided with a truck. While the opinion on the injury was pending on the MLC, IO searched for eye witness. One Mohd. Azruddin, s/o Mohd. MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 2 of 29 ss Jainuddin informed to be brother of the victim. An FIR u/s 279/337 of IPC was registered and the matter was investigated. During investigation, IO returned to the spot, seized the scooty, prepared a site plan however no eye witness was found. During that time, a telephonic intimation was received regarding haulting of the offending truck bearing no. DL-1LV-8344. Offending truck and its documents were seized and Respondent no.1 was arrested. 3. Upon completion of investigation DAR was filed before this Court while chargesheet was filed before concerned Ld. Magistrate. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver cum owner, Respondent no.2 is insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured. 5. In response to the DAR, Respondent no.2 filed its reply denying the occurrence of the accident or involvement of the offending vehicle. It is pleaded that the accident, if any, occurred due to sole negligence of the claimant. It is pleaded that the petitioner did not have a driving licence and was driving his vehicle without a helmet, in violation of traffic rules. It is thus submitted that the Insurance company/Respondent no.2 is not liable to indemnify the insured i.e. Respondent no.1 or compensate the petitioner. Despite opportunity Respondent no. 1 did not file any reply. Page no. 3 of 29 ss 6. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 12.04.2019. OPP. 3. Relief. Mustafa Kamal (Dar) vs Ajeet Singh (254/18 New Friends Colony) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87512516/ 2 7. During trial, disability certificate noticing 30% visual disability, 48% with respect to Neuropsychological and total disability of injured as 62% was received. 8. In order to prove the claim, petitioner examined himself as PW1. PW-1/petitioner Sh. Mustafa Kamal tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-1/1. He further relied upon DAR as Ex.PW1/2(colly), discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/3(colly), MLC as Ex.PW-1/4, Treatment Records as Ex.PW-1/5(colly), Original Medical bills as ExPW-1/6(colly), permanent disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/7, Salary certificate as Ex.PW-1/8(colly), Statement of NRE Bank account as Ex.PW- 1/9(colly), copy of 10th Class certificate/age proof as Ex.PW- 1/10(OSR), copy of passport, resident identity proof, copy of Aadhar card and two driving licences as Ex.PW-1/11(colly) Page no. 4 of 29 ss (OSR). He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.2/insurance company. 9. No evidence led on behalf of any of the Respondents. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner/ claimant/applicant and against the respondents. (iii) Loss of amenities of life : The Rs.20,000/- petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.
texts.arguments: 11. It has been argued on behalf of the petitioner that the factum of accident due to negligence of Respondent no.1 has been duly proved. It is argued that the petitioner has proved his income at the time of accident to be 10,000/- Saudi Riyal per month (which was at exchange rate of Rs.19 in 2019 i.e. Rs.1,90,000/-p.m.). It is argued that due to the injury suffered in the accident, petitioner has sustained 62% total disability and has lost his job. It is thus argued that the petitioner be compensated accordingly. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.2 has argued that the claim of the petitioner is suspicious in as much as the IO has filed two charge sheets in the case, the initial one not reflecting any witness to the accident while the other citing one Gurvinder Singh as the person who haulted the offending vehicle. It is submitted that even the arrest memo initially filed with the present DAR did not reveal the time of arrest, which goes to show that the offending vehicle has been planted by the Investigating officer in collusion of the petitioner as well as MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 5 of 29 ss driver cum owner of such vehicle. It is argued that there is no eye witness to the accident and the fact that the petitioner was brought unconscious to the hospital, there was no occasion for such petitioner to have identified or revealed the registration number of the offending vehicle to the investigating officer or the person who allegedly haulted the same. It is further argued that though the accident allegedly occurred at 01:00 AM, the photographs filed by the IO of the offending truck and of the scooty of the petitioner, are of day time. It is submitted that even the FIR has been lodged in the morning hours despite claimant that the offending vehicle was seized soon after the accident. It is submitted that the person namely Gurvinder Singh has not been examined as a witness in the present case and there is no connecting link to show as to how the investigating officer came to know about the accident. It is further submitted that as per information available to Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.2, petitioner and Respondent no.1 have collusively Mustafa Kamal (Dar) vs Ajeet Singh (254/18 New Friends Colony) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87512516/ 3 compounded the criminal proceedings before Ld.MM. It is further argued that even the proof of income filed by the petitioner is not reliable as there is no certainty in the amount he had been receiving in his account as salary and for the reason that the employer has not been examined to prove the salary certificate. It is argued that the record relied upon by the petitioner shows that the petitioner was not permanently working at Saudi Arabia and that there is no justification for his presence in India at the time of accident. It is thus argued that the claim of the petitioner be rejected. In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. It has been held in National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 17. PW-1, during his cross examination has further stated that he had seen the registration number of the offending truck and denied to have been negligent himself. Even if it is assumed that the petitioner was not wearing a helmet, it has been held in United India Insurance Company v. Smt. Najma (decided on 18.11.2020) by Hon'ble Delhi High Court that mere not wearing of a helmet would not amount to contributory negligence. Thus, even the MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 9 of 29 ss argument of contributory negligence on the part of petitioner is not proved. 20. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 10 of 29 ss that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Mustafa Kamal (Dar) vs Ajeet Singh (254/18 New Friends Colony) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87512516/ 5 Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 21. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure; MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no . 11 of 29 ss (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising; (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 22. 25. Reliance is placed on judgment of Hon'ble Kerala High Court in Valsamma and Anr. vs. Binu Jose and ors. (2014 (1) KHC207) wherein it was held that where the deceased, aged 29 years was working as spray painter in Oman, and was having visa upto 25.03.2005 while the accident took place on18.09.2004, his employment agreement, labour card or passport were not sufficient to prove that the deceased was having an income of Rs.20,000/- per month. The Division Bench noticed that, employment in Gulf Countries is not certain and it is likely to be terminated at any time. If the deceased was a permanent employee there, then that can be taken as permanent income and that may be useful to assess the compensation payable to his dependents on that basis. So, in such circumstances, the court will have to assess the income of the person, in the context of Indian standards, taking the probable income which he may have fetched if he was working in India during the relevant time and the income which he was alleged to have been earning in a Gulf MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 17 of 29 ss Country where the employment of such nature is not permanent and is likely to be terminated at the whims and fancies of the sponsored cannot be relied upon. 26. Further, in Abraham Jacob @ Avarachan vs. N. Mubarak & ors. (2014 (3) KLT883), it was held that though the salary certificate showing monthly income of Qatari Riyal 10,000/- (equivalent INR 1,15,000/-) was authenticated by the Counsular Officer of the Embassy of India at Doha (Qatar), in accordance with the provisions under the Diplomatic and Counsular Officer (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948 the same would not dispensed with the proof of a document according the law if it is to be used as evidence in a Court of Law. The court further held that all that Section 3 of the Act does is to enable a court to dispensed with the proof of genuineness of the seal and signatures of a diplomatic or counsular officer on a particular document. The court further observed that although the salary certificate is a document authenticated in accordance of Section 3 of the Act, the monthly income of Qatari Riyal 10,000/- shown in that certificate cannot be taken as the basis for calculating compensation payable under various heads. MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 18 of 29 ss Similar view was taken by Hon'ble Kerala High Court in Maimoonammal Arif vs. Ponnan.M.A (MACA no. 2139/2010 decided on 25.02.2020) wherein at the time of accident the deceased was claimed to be working as a manager of a shop at Saudi Arabia. The court, relying on the judgment of Sherfuddin vs. Saveesh K. Mustafa Kamal (Dar) vs Ajeet Singh (254/18 New Friends Colony) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87512516/ 9 & anr. (2014 (1) KHC242) and Satheesan E.K. vs. Musthafa K.P. & anr. (2018 (5) KHC884) held that the income alleged to have been earned by a person in a foreign country cannot be taken as such for the purpose of assessing his monthly income. The court has to consider the standards in India as to what would have been the probable income that such a person will earn if he was employed here. 34. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for Mustafa Kamal (Dar) vs Ajeet Singh (254/18 New Friends Colony) on 1 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87512516/ 12 effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and the demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society MACT No: 20/19 Mustafa Kamal v. Ajeet Singh & ors. Page no. 24 of 29 ss to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
